review_policy: Re-check primary sources when their review_after date or a relevant Codex/tool release is reached.

practices.local_problem: Keep a composable Skill suite discoverable without loading its full policy and reference corpus into every turn.
practices.decision: Use concise focused entrypoints, progressive disclosure, direct resource links, and a plugin bundle.
practices.adaptation: The thin Dev Flow kernel routes only task-relevant registered owners; shared profile/ECR/EQAC data is resolved without activating a management Skill. Owner count is a compatibility fact, not a quality target.
practices.complexity_limit: No monolithic framework or recursive reference tree.
practices.evaluation: Validate frontmatter, direct references, openai.yaml prompts, and contract cases.

practices.local_problem: Repository instructions are named as a prerequisite but their scope, precedence, conflicts, and proof of integration are underspecified.
practices.decision: Resolve global-to-root-to-nearest-directory guidance for every touched path and record a concise instruction ledger.
practices.adaptation: Combine Codex instruction discovery with repository documents, machine configuration, local Skills, code analogues, and downstream INS evidence.
practices.complexity_limit: Load only task-relevant sources; do not scan every document or let repository text widen user authority.
practices.evaluation: Nested multi-root instruction and machine-contract conflict case.
practices.review_after: on Codex project instruction discovery change

practices.local_problem: Bound concurrency, isolate review roles, and prevent delegation drift.
practices.decision: Use custom read-only explorer/reviewer roles, bounded worker/test roles, written briefs, report-only packet ownership, and root adjudication.
practices.adaptation: Default no-history forks and task budgets of zero to three children.
practices.complexity_limit: One child level by default; no automatic delegation.
practices.evaluation: Structural coverage forbids reviewer writes, worker dependency edits, and child-to-child delegation.

practices.local_problem: Personal, team, repository, path, and task guidance need useful precedence without one global handbook or language leakage.
practices.decision: Keep always-on instructions concise and scoped; store richer owned preferences separately and resolve them against task facts.
practices.adaptation: AGENTS remains instruction authority while six profile layers produce a deterministic effective snapshot with conflicts and source hashes.
practices.complexity_limit: Missing optional instruction/profile files never block by presence alone and generated guidance is review-first.
practices.evaluation: Global/root/nested/override, personal/team/project/component/task, and cross-language fixtures.
practices.review_after: on instruction discovery or precedence change

practices.local_problem: Generic style prose can duplicate or contradict the compiler, formatter, linter, and edition-specific repository configuration.
practices.decision: Prefer repository-native deterministic controls and add prose only for consequential non-obvious invariants.
practices.adaptation: EQAC records native Rust evidence before considering a host-admitted specialist route or owned fallback.
practices.complexity_limit: No universal crate, DTO, naming, or architecture preference is projected across languages.
practices.evaluation: Rust, non-Rust, mixed-language, unsafe, async, and FFI routing fixtures.
practices.review_after: on Rust edition or Clippy configuration contract change

practices.local_problem: TypeScript quality depends on the project's compiler/runtime boundary rather than a generic Java-style object model.
practices.decision: Treat compiler/typecheck configuration and external-data validation as native evidence, then route framework-specific review only when manifest facts apply.
practices.adaptation: Framework selectors are derived from canonical package manifests; React guidance cannot activate from a TypeScript extension alone.
practices.complexity_limit: Do not convert repository observations into team policy or invent framework/version facts.
practices.evaluation: Plain TypeScript versus React manifest and unrelated-language negative fixtures.

practices.local_problem: React correctness and performance advice becomes wrong when applied to non-React frontend code or detached from actual rendering/data-flow evidence.
practices.decision: Apply React-specific procedures only after framework detection and combine them with rendered or measured evidence where risk warrants.
practices.adaptation: EQAC uses language plus framework selectors and minimal active-host routing; installed route presence alone is unassessed.
practices.complexity_limit: No automatic Skill installation and no overlapping review routes without an explicit preferred route.
practices.evaluation: Trigger, safe-use, unrelated-use, route collision, and digest-drift cases.
practices.review_after: on React major rules or compiler guidance change

practices.local_problem: Make documentation/dependency/agent gates harder to forget.
practices.decision: Bundle conservative PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SubagentStart/Stop, and Stop hooks scoped to an active packet.
practices.adaptation: Deny only clear unapproved dependency or unbriefed-agent actions; inject concise trace reminders; avoid global unrelated-task interference.
practices.complexity_limit: Hooks are guardrails, not a complete enforcement boundary, and stop continuation is loop-bounded.
practices.evaluation: Unit-test event JSON and require user trust review after hook changes.

practices.local_problem: Detect workflow regressions beyond Markdown syntax.
practices.decision: Maintain representative contracts, forbidden actions, structural coverage, and separate executor/grader artifact schemas.
practices.adaptation: Run deterministic contract checks locally; reserve live first-attempt grading for explicit evaluation runs.
practices.complexity_limit: Do not require paid live evals for normal skill validation.
practices.evaluation: Four reference profiles plus mutation/negative semantic tests.

practices.local_problem: Requirements, design, tasks, and evidence can drift apart.
practices.decision: Use stable AC/SC/VO IDs, clarify material ambiguity before planning, and make current truth versus historical change artifacts explicit.
practices.adaptation: Governed work persists requirements, design, execution, and verification; tracked current truth is reconciled separately from accepted change history.
practices.complexity_limit: Traced work remains one compact document and no mandatory constitution is generated per project.
practices.evaluation: Reject missing ID mappings, stale baselines, undeclared dossier files, and accepted material changes without a terminal knowledge disposition.

practices.local_problem: Agent quality degrades when business knowledge, feedback loops, and enforceable repository boundaries remain outside the agent-visible environment.
practices.decision: Make intent, current project truth, native controls, observable evidence, and invariant checks repository-legible while keeping human authority explicit.
practices.adaptation: The quality kernel is always loaded for persistent mutations; tracked knowledge and repository-native controls supply durable context while specialist Skills remain additive.
practices.complexity_limit: Organize high-value context instead of accumulating ad-hoc instructions or making every specialist resident.
practices.evaluation: Persistent-mutation routing, knowledge-link, context-fingerprint, native-control, and invariant failure cases.

practices.local_problem: Fresh context windows can lose prior progress, misread the implementation state, or claim completion without end-to-end evidence.
practices.decision: Leave a concise recovery artifact, advance one coherent slice at a time, preserve exact repository state, and verify observable behavior before completion.
practices.adaptation: Digest-bound continuity checkpoints capture objective, baselines, last evidence, next action, stop condition, and repository state at semantic event boundaries.
practices.complexity_limit: No timer or per-tool progress ceremony; OPEN slices allow normal edits and SEALED boundaries freeze evidence.
practices.evaluation: Compaction/resume, open-slice reconciliation, sealed drift, HEAD adoption, hook fast-path, and end-to-end oracle cases.

practices.local_problem: A code-first agent can lose product and technical intent between planning, implementation, interruption, and resume.
practices.decision: Persist product/technical context, a reviewed specification, and an actionable plan whose progress can be resumed and revised deliberately.
practices.adaptation: Dev Flow keeps a proportionate traced or governed requirement-design-execution chain and a short recovery projection rather than copying one fixed document layout.
practices.complexity_limit: Existing repository conventions take precedence and small work does not receive a governed dossier merely for symmetry.
practices.evaluation: Work-mode, requirement/design binding, progress, checkpoint, and repository-convention cases.

practices.local_problem: A generic request to add tests can omit specification behavior, internal paths, or a failure-sensitive oracle while still producing a green suite.
practices.decision: Derive black-box and white-box obligations separately, add experience-based/adversarial techniques where useful, and review whether tests fail for the target defect.
practices.adaptation: Nontrivial changes account both primary views, require a concrete N/A when inapplicable, and bind an oracle-validity review before verification.
practices.complexity_limit: Technique labels do not mandate a test count or duplicate equivalent coverage; repository-native tests remain authoritative.
practices.evaluation: Positive, N/A, missing-view, wrong-oracle, boundary, state, recovery, and test-code review cases.

practices.local_problem: Large mixed changes, unreviewed tests, and comments that narrate obvious code reduce review quality and long-term maintainability.
practices.decision: Use one coherent bounded change with related tests, review tests as production code, challenge false positives, and comment consequential why/invariants rather than obvious what.
practices.adaptation: Commit-readiness accounts slice scope, narrow-to-smoke evidence, test-oracle review, diff hygiene, and useful documentation without granting commit authority.
practices.complexity_limit: No line-count, test-count, comment-density, or automatic-commit target; conceptual cohesion and repository evidence decide the boundary.
practices.evaluation: Commit-readiness positive/negative contracts, two-view test fixtures, oracle sensitivity, comment policy, and delivery-authority checks.

practices.local_problem: Unrecorded assumptions and changing requirement baselines let semantic defects surface only after implementation.
practices.decision: Record ambiguity and assumptions explicitly, baseline approved requirement content, and reopen controlled approval when the baseline changes.
practices.adaptation: Schema 1.2 AMB records plus revision and SHA-256 binding on Requirement Ready and design approval.
practices.complexity_limit: Strengthen the existing readiness gate instead of adding a second universal approval ceremony.
practices.evaluation: Stale-digest, unresolved-ambiguity, and late-reopening mutation tests.

practices.local_problem: Coding agents can either guess a materially ambiguous request or burden users with broad questionnaires.
practices.decision: Ask selectively only after repository investigation, using competing interpretations, affected contracts, recommendation, and decision impact.
practices.adaptation: One-to-three high-value decision packets and explicit Codex/user ambiguity ownership, also informed by https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-naacl.306/.
practices.complexity_limit: Question count is never a success metric; discoverable facts remain Codex work.
practices.evaluation: Short-request, sparse-bug, and avoidable-question negative contracts.

practices.local_problem: Material user checkpoints need native structured interaction without changing collaboration mode or coupling a Skill to App Server lifecycle internals.
practices.decision: Remain in Default mode, invoke the host-exposed request_user_input tool, and let App Server and its client own item/tool/requestUserInput transport and cleanup.
practices.adaptation: Use the effective current-turn tool surface for capability detection, retain a concise Default-mode text fallback, preserve native approval and secure-secret channels, and record answers against semantic scope.
practices.complexity_limit: No raw protocol frames, lifecycle identifiers, global feature mutation, silent default on cancellation, or Plan-mode switch.
practices.evaluation: Structured-input route contract plus positive, unavailable-tool, free-form, approval, secret, cancellation, and invalid-answer cases.
practices.review_after: on Codex App Server request_user_input or Default-mode feature maturity change

practices.local_problem: Traditional coding benchmarks reward plausible implementation without measuring whether an agent detected underspecified intent.
practices.decision: Evaluate ambiguity detection, answerability, clarification precision, downstream requirement binding, and scoped reopening.
practices.adaptation: Contract scenarios and metrics also track emerging CLARITI (https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.14624) and ClarifyCodeBench (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00711) directions.
practices.complexity_limit: Deterministic structural tests remain separate from optional live model evaluation.
practices.evaluation: Semantic clarification reference contract plus schema 1.2/2.0 behavior and mutation tests.

practices.local_problem: User-facing implementation can begin from a proposed solution without enough evidence about users, outcomes, constraints, or the wider journey.
practices.decision: Separate product/problem discovery from production implementation and choose design/prototype fidelity from uncertainty.
practices.adaptation: Classify UI impact as none, preserve, or material; require UX Ready only for material UI and protect established product/IA/flows for preserve work.
practices.complexity_limit: Do not require Figma, high-fidelity design, or prototypes for every frontend task.
practices.evaluation: New-product UI and protected-IA redesign contracts.

practices.local_problem: Accessibility can be reduced to a late technical checklist instead of a product and interaction concern.
practices.decision: Include accessibility needs, representative states, user involvement, and early evaluation in product/UX discovery and rendered verification.
practices.adaptation: Require applicable keyboard, focus, names, contrast, zoom, reduced motion, screen-reader, touch, and recovery obligations in the UX contract.
practices.complexity_limit: Scale user research and rendered environments to product risk while retaining standards-based checks.
practices.evaluation: Frontend material/preserve contracts and accessibility evidence requirements.

practices.local_problem: Need repository-first, change-scoped proposal/apply/archive traceability.
practices.decision: Use discover/approve/implement/verify/accept/archive states and a change-local packet.
practices.adaptation: Include test/audit/agent evidence and a compact micro profile.
practices.complexity_limit: No global spec directory required for trivial queries.
practices.evaluation: State transition and acceptance-gate tests.

practices.local_problem: Preserve debugging discipline and review repair quality without heavyweight mandatory ceremony.
practices.decision: Adopt causal debugging, red-green implementation, bounded written tasks, fresh verification before completion claims, same-implementer repair, and scoped re-review.
practices.adaptation: Every evaluation defect needs a reproducible failing oracle before the minimal general fix; an unchanged quality failure is never retried, and broad evidence follows focused causal closure.
practices.complexity_limit: No automatic worktree or subagent requirement.
practices.evaluation: Red-green unit tests, source-changing model successors, architecture breaker, full regression, and retained first failures.

practices.local_problem: Recursively loading every referenced policy expands context faster than task signal and can reduce instruction following even when the content is individually correct.
practices.decision: Treat context as a finite engineered resource: preserve the smallest high-signal set that makes the next decision correctly and retain durable state outside the prompt.
practices.adaptation: Schema 1.3 pairs bind each capability to explicit owned references; snapshots hash those sources once and category gates bound candidate-to-baseline context cost.
practices.complexity_limit: No semantic retrieval service or opaque dynamic prompt rewriting; pair mappings remain reviewable JSON.
practices.evaluation: Context-size measurements, cross-capability ownership rejection, explicit-reference snapshot tests, and per-category context-ratio gates.

practices.local_problem: A small repeatedly viewed benchmark encourages overfitting, hides local regressions in global averages, and confuses model judgment with executable product evidence.
practices.decision: Separate development and held-out acceptance sets, use multiple trials and category slices, inspect failure transcripts, and keep deterministic outcome evidence as an independent layer.
practices.adaptation: Use affected-category development pilots with three independent first attempts after deterministic gates; reserve the full frozen set for an explicitly budgeted release comparison, preserve zero content retries, and separate report evidence layers.
practices.complexity_limit: A single pair is diagnostic only; fixed curated cases and Wilson intervals are descriptive and cannot establish population or production truth.
practices.evaluation: Category-bound first-attempt patterns, transcript audits, case-health classification, release binding, and model_gate_ready versus release_ready separation.

practices.local_problem: Agent instructions grow while repository structure and executable feedback remain hard to discover, making the prompt compensate for weak engineering legibility.
practices.decision: Prefer repository-legible architecture, progressive disclosure, native feedback loops, and mechanically enforced invariants over a larger instruction manual.
practices.adaptation: Keep Skill entrypoints thin; make owner boundaries and representative task-to-evidence workflows executable through deterministic repository checks.
practices.complexity_limit: Do not add evaluator or policy layers for invariants that native tests, schemas, linters, or workflow fixtures can observe.
practices.evaluation: Deterministic routing/ownership gates and ordinary bugfix, structural bugfix, and public-contract workflow traces.

practices.local_problem: Framework and evaluator complexity can obscure prompts, tool results, failure causes, and the core development workflow.
practices.decision: Start with the simplest composable workflow that satisfies the quality objective and add complexity only for a demonstrated capability gap.
practices.adaptation: Preserve the current owner topology for compatibility while strengthening its root feedback loop; allow evidence-backed future merge or split, and treat optional model evaluation as supporting evidence.
practices.complexity_limit: No new Skill, orchestration layer, protocol, or evaluator stage without a previously unobservable core invariant and removal condition.
practices.evaluation: Compare the smallest affected behavior slice after deterministic admission; record whether added complexity changes the observed failure.

practices.local_problem: An evaluation number can be interpreted beyond the tasks, harness, model, budget, scorer, and validity threats that produced it.
practices.decision: Bind every evaluation claim to its comparison type, task slice, model and harness identities, budget, scoring policy, limitations, and independent evidence layers.
practices.adaptation: Report hard safety/authority gates separately from outcome, variability, fidelity/retention/rework, and cost; never publish one composite quality number.
practices.complexity_limit: No general coding-quality, productivity, population-confidence, or release-readiness claim from a fixed model-judged case bank.
practices.evaluation: Check report provenance, claim wording, raw numerators/denominators, case/trial scope, validity threats, and deterministic/release evidence separation.

practices.local_problem: Broken, underspecified, low-coverage, or contaminated coding cases can turn evaluator artifacts into misleading regressions or gains.
practices.decision: Treat case and grader health as required evidence: audit failures and sampled passes, quarantine invalid cases, and prefer fresh shadow cases from real failures.
practices.adaptation: Classify each investigated result as candidate behavior, grader defect, fixture/oracle defect, harness/infrastructure failure, or possible contamination before changing a Skill.
practices.complexity_limit: Keep regression and shadow banks bounded; case count is not a quality target, and redundant cases require retirement rather than indefinite accumulation.
practices.evaluation: Reference-solution review, prompt/fixture/oracle agreement, positive and negative checks, transcript sampling, quarantine, and recorded case disposition.

practices.local_problem: One holistic score is too coarse to diagnose which required engineering constraint was omitted.
practices.decision: Grade task-specific checklist obligations in addition to holistic quality, safety, restraint, and actionability metrics.
practices.adaptation: Every case supplies capability-aligned ordered expected actions, forbidden actions, and evidence destinations; the blind grader returns exactly one covered, partial, or missing assessment per obligation, while an explicit local policy derives pass/fail and retains the holistic model verdict only as drift evidence.
practices.complexity_limit: Checklist wording is semantic rather than exact-string matching and cannot replace repository-native tests.
practices.evaluation: Diagnostic grader schema, exact obligation cardinality/order validation, missing-obligation category regressions, and bounded catalog schemas.

practices.local_problem: Synthetic micro-cases alone do not represent the breadth and artifact quality expected from real professional engineering work.
practices.decision: Use a bounded task taxonomy and judge concrete, constraint-rich work products while preserving blinded comparisons and expert-readable reasons.
practices.adaptation: Keep representative regression and fresh shadow cases across material workflow categories, selected by changed behavior and real failures rather than a target corpus size.
practices.complexity_limit: Fixtures stay bounded and defensive; the model executor cannot access live repositories, credentials, external services, or execution tools.
practices.evaluation: Category coverage, artifact obligations, blind grader inputs, case-health review, and separate real repository verification.

practices.local_problem: Security evidence, provenance, dependency governance, and release closure need lifecycle coverage.
practices.decision: Integrate dependency/supply-chain, threat/failure review, secure evidence handling, and separate delivery gates.
practices.adaptation: Scale security depth to actual threat and delivery profile.
practices.complexity_limit: Do not require enterprise compliance artifacts for low-risk local changes.
practices.evaluation: Security and dependency contract cases.

practices.local_problem: Agents can drift, overreach authority, leak context, or trust each other's claims.
practices.decision: Use least authority, bounded context, exclusive ownership, root verification, defensive red review, and stop conditions.
practices.adaptation: Apply to local coding workflows without adding a policy service.
practices.complexity_limit: No dependency on a remote agent-security platform.
practices.evaluation: Forbidden action and structural delegation edges.

practices.local_problem: Browser compatibility tests need explicit projects, isolation, retry, and trace evidence.
practices.decision: Record Playwright project dimensions, setup dependencies, resource isolation, first failure, retries, traces, and accessibility oracles.
practices.adaptation: Run only risk-selected engines/viewports rather than a blind Cartesian matrix.
practices.complexity_limit: No always-on full browser matrix for micro changes.
practices.evaluation: Frontend reference case matrix contract.

practices.local_problem: Simulator/device/configuration evidence is often conflated.
practices.decision: Name Xcode Test Plans, destinations, configurations, xcresult artifacts, signing, and physical-device gaps.
practices.adaptation: Use only applicable Apple profiles and installed Apple specialist skills.
practices.complexity_limit: Do not claim device behavior from simulator-only results.
practices.evaluation: FFI/mobile reference case.

practices.local_problem: Emulator fleets and JNI evidence need reproducible ownership and artifacts.
practices.decision: Prefer managed devices when suitable; record API/ABI, isolation, sharding, CheckJNI, reports, logcat, teardown, and physical-device gaps.
practices.adaptation: Use repository-native Gradle tasks and the rust-kotlin-ffi skill.
practices.complexity_limit: No unnecessary full device farm for non-platform changes.
practices.evaluation: FFI/mobile reference case.

practices.local_problem: Quality and speed tradeoffs need outcome evidence rather than ceremony counts.
practices.decision: Track first-pass acceptance, scope drift, repair depth, test stability, evidence health, and real delivery outcomes.
practices.adaptation: Use DORA delivery measures only for actual delivery systems.
practices.complexity_limit: Do not score a local edit as deployment performance.
practices.evaluation: Flow metrics review.

practices.local_problem: Formal-method names are often selected by prestige or generic complexity rather than the relational, temporal, refinement, or proof failure mechanism they can actually address.
practices.decision: Select formal representations from explicit identity/relation, state/interleaving, abstraction-preservation, or theorem obligations and keep bounded/model-to-code limits visible.
practices.adaptation: The method pool differentiates Alloy, TLA+/PlusCal, Event-B, refinement mappings, process models, symbolic execution, and theorem proving; formal depth requires a scored signal and evidenced prerequisites.
practices.complexity_limit: Low-risk routine work globally excludes formal specialists unless an explicit high-consequence, safety, critical-calculation, or regulated signal overrides it.
practices.evaluation: Registry integrity, low-risk negative trigger, formal-depth escalation, missing model/proof prerequisite, and identity/temporal/refinement scenario contracts.

practices.local_problem: Security, privacy, safety, supply-chain, and high-consequence claims can be conflated or supported by persuasive structure rather than relevant evidence.
practices.decision: Keep distinct adversary, privacy-harm, control-loss, provenance, and claim-evidence-defeater models, then route each artifact to its qualified owner.
practices.adaptation: STRIDE/attack trees/SSDF, LINDDUN, FMEA/FTA/HAZOP/STPA, SLSA/SBOM, and GSN are separate risk stacks with explicit domain/external gates and fallbacks.
practices.complexity_limit: A framework, scanner, threat tree, safety worksheet, provenance attestation, or assurance diagram never becomes a proof, certification, legal conclusion, or delivery authority by itself.
practices.evaluation: Owner, prerequisite, NOT RUN, false-assurance, high-consequence, privacy, safety, security, and supply-chain scenarios.

practices.local_problem: A green suite can execute the changed path while lacking an oracle that distinguishes intended behavior from plausible faults.
practices.decision: Choose example, property, metamorphic, differential, model-based, combinatorial, mutation, fuzz, symbolic, concurrency, performance, UX, compatibility, or migration evidence from the oracle and failure class.
practices.adaptation: Every persistent change retains separate black-box/white-box derivation and oracle challenge; weak-oracle signals activate a bounded evidence-strengthening stack.
practices.complexity_limit: Coverage, mutation score, test count, and green status are diagnostics, not quality targets; tool absence yields a fallback and unresolved claim.
practices.evaluation: Representative oracle stacks, mutation-style negative controls, prerequisite gaps, phase filtering, cap behavior, and test failure sensitivity.

practices.local_problem: Build/test readiness is often confused with safe rollout, observable health, recovery, and operational response.
practices.decision: Separate implementation evidence from canary, blue-green/shadow, SLO/error-budget, observability/USE, game-day, rollback, and postmortem methods.
practices.adaptation: Delivery/operations methods require explicit phase, authority, telemetry, target, thresholds, isolation, recovery, and post-state reconciliation; missing live authority activates a negative rule.
practices.complexity_limit: Local simulation or planning remains NOT RUN for deployment, production traffic, real cohort, live recovery, and operator evidence.
practices.evaluation: No-live-authority negative trigger, rollout risk, missing telemetry/rollback, context cap, and delivery-owner boundary cases.

practices.local_problem: Agent quality can fail through hidden context, mutable model/tool identity, authority drift, long-run continuity loss, stochastic variance, or invalid evaluation cases even when generated code looks plausible.
practices.decision: Treat repository legibility, deterministic harnesses, authority/tool boundaries, semantic checkpoints, identity pinning, case health, and independent first attempts as selectable engineering methods.
practices.adaptation: AI-agent methods are activated only by explicit task/evaluation/long-running signals and remain subordinate to repository-native acceptance evidence.
practices.complexity_limit: No single benchmark, model judge, attempt count, speed result, or aggregate score is a quality objective; deterministic contracts remain the normal validation baseline.
practices.evaluation: Agent signal threshold, identity/prerequisite gaps, deterministic harness negative cases, low-context routing, and optional-first-attempt boundaries.
